messages.subject: Re: Error deploying: mkdir: too many links
parts:
As of about 5 hours ago several of the students from the Coursera Developing Data Products course have been experiencing the same error message. 

Using:
shinyapps::deployApp()

Gives the following error message:

Uploading bundle for application: 47762...DONE
Deploying bundle: 207260 for application: 47762 ...
Waiting for task: 45565994
  building: Parsing manifest
  building: Fetching packages
  error: Installing packages
################################## Begin Log ################################## 
################################### End Log ################################### 
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 45565995 error: Unhandled Exception: mkdir /mnt/docker/volumes/5976449d1fde0f0eb63ff5c83b67a295c79c7af62aefdda39e332c1fe465026a: too many links


The task and application numbers are different in each case, but the message is the same in each case. 

As with Rick Aster, Several of the students have reported that attempting to deploy the app again at a different time lets them publish without the error.
 
Elsewhere on the internet it suggests that the mkdir - too many links error message is related to there being too many subdirectories. There definitely isn't too many subdirectories in my shiny app (there is only one data subdirectory, and there are less than 10 files total in the app adding up to about 2Mb of space). 

Is it possible that more people signed up through www.shinyapps.io/coursera than expected, and too many subdirectories were created for their projects? 

Ronny.

messages.author: a0eb7ab2abe1a8ef
messages.subject: Re: Error deploying: mkdir: too many links
parts: Im a Coursera student also facing this issue. Its worth noting that the issue is NOT on your local side, ie it doesnt matter how many folders you have on your hard-drive. Shinyapps.io is apparently setting up a new folder for you when you deploy, and the volume they store the account folders in is full. I expect anyone who has published previously can keep doing so, unless its project folders not account folders. Since you mention some students able to "get through" the error, this would suggest either they had a different issue or there are several volumes it may try to put your folder on and not all of them are full yet. I would suggest to the JH@Coursera staff that the solution is NOT to fail everyone who cant post, and to the students please dont just hammer away at shineyapps.io. This is a bug that they need to fix and waiting for that is the only real way around it.
